What comes up in Seven Hills

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Warehouse demolition with the slab and hardstand

Seven Hills industrial sites usually have more concrete than building, and the hardstand is frequently the larger part of the job.

How it is handled
Structure removed first, then the slab and hardstand broken out and crushed so clean concrete is reused rather than landfilled.
What does it
Large excavator with a shear or grapple, hydraulic hammer, truck and dogs for volume.

Working beside a trading tenancy

Industrial estates here are rarely empty, so the neighbours keep operating through the work.

How it is handled
Hoarding, dust and noise control, agreed hours, and a sequence that keeps the neighbouring access open throughout.
What does it
Machines sized to the hoarded area rather than the site, with water for dust control.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Seven Hills

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Industrial and residential side by side Warehouse and factory demolition a few streets from suburban knockdowns, with very different surveys and waste streams.
  • Steel and concrete recycling On industrial sites the separation is a real part of the value rather than a formality.
  • Unknown fill on older industrial land Which is worth testing before the dig is priced.
  • Good truck access on the industrial streets Built for it, which helps the cartage considerably.

The industrial parts of Seven Hills are set up for heavy vehicles, so cartage is rarely the constraint. On the residential side the usual side access limits apply. Where neighbouring tenancies keep operating through a demolition, the hoarding, the dust control and the hours are planned around them.

Seven Hills questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish warehouses and factories?
Yes. It is licensed work and it runs as a sequence: hazardous materials survey, service disconnections, soft strip, then the structure, with steel and concrete separated as it comes down.
What about the concrete hardstand and the slab?
Both can come out and both are recyclable. Clean concrete is crushed and reused rather than landfilled, which is usually the cheaper outcome as well as the better one.
Do you charge travel to come out to Western Sydney?
No. Western Sydney is one of the two areas we are in most weeks, so there is no travel loading on work here and a site visit is usually easy to arrange.
Does the asbestos work sit under your demolition licence?
No. Demolition licence AD214737 covers the structure. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and clearance by an independent licensed assessor, because the assessor has to be independent of whoever did the removal. All of it is scheduled as a single job.
